Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

The current PR (#27658) fixes the crash with a size-based guard (skip diff if content > 512 KB). This is minimal and safe to merge, but there is a more principled approach worth considering as a follow-up.

**Root distinction: binary vs large text**

The real problem is that binary files (images, archives, executables) should never be diffed at all — a unified diff of binary content is meaningless and can be arbitrarily large. Large *text* files, on the other hand, still have meaningful diffs; we just shouldn't store the full thing.

A cleaner solution would be:

```typescript
function isBinary(content: string): boolean {
  return content.includes('\0') // null byte is the standard binary heuristic
}

function safeDiff(oldContent: string, newContent: string, filePath: string): string {
  if (isBinary(oldContent) || isBinary(newContent)) return ""

  const diff = createTwoFilesPatch(filePath, filePath, oldContent, newContent)
  const MAX_LINES = 500
  const lines = diff.split('\n')
  if (lines.length <= MAX_LINES) return diff
  return lines.slice(0, MAX_LINES).join('\n') + `\n... (${lines.length - MAX_LINES} more lines)`
}
```

This approach:
- Skips diff generation entirely for binary files (before calling `createTwoFilesPatch`, so no wasted CPU/memory)
- Preserves partial diffs for large text files instead of discarding them completely
- Applies consistently across all call sites in `edit.ts` and `apply_patch.ts`

The trade-off is a slightly larger diff (~30–40 lines touching all call sites) vs the current PR (~9 lines). Happy to leave this to maintainer judgment — the crash fix in #27658 is the priority.

We have a similar multi-tenant use case but need to go one step further.
Not only do we need per-session auth headers, we need per-session MCP 
server lists — different users should see different MCP servers entirely
based on their role.

A more complete solution would be supporting a full `mcp` config in 
POST /session (not just `mcpAuth`), which would cover both use cases:
- Different auth tokens per user (your use case)
- Different MCP servers per user (our use case)

Related: #6822 (agentId in POST /session)

## Confirmed on v1.15.0 + Windows 11 (with full crash trace)

Still reproducible on **OpenCode Desktop v1.15.0** (released 2026-05-15), **Windows 11 x64**.

### Crash Trace

From sidecar log (`share/log/2026-05-15T045357.log`):

\\\
ERROR service=session.processor session.id=ses_xxxx messageID=msg_xxxx error=Aborted stack=AbortError: Aborted
    at new DOMException (node:internal/per_context/domexception:76:18)
    at Array.<anonymous> (node-CDG1DJG7.js:293605:27)
    at Generator.next (<anonymous>)
    at ~effect/Effect/successCont (node-CDG1DJG7.js:7907:29)
    at ~effect/Effect/evaluate (node-CDG1DJG7.js:7921:25)
    at FiberImpl.runLoop (node-CDG1DJG7.js:7733:112)
    at FiberImpl.evaluate (node-CDG1DJG7.js:7703:26)
\\\

### Crash Pattern

- Sidecar starts normally, serves requests
- After completing a conversation turn (LLM response + tool calls), the \session.processor\ throws an unhandled \AbortError\
- Sidecar exits with code 1
- OpenCode auto-restarts sidecar, but all in-progress context is lost

### Timeline from main.log

\\\
[12:53:55] sidecar started
[12:55:46] sidecar exited { code: 1 }  // ~2 min after first request
[12:56:51] sidecar exited { code: 1 }  // second crash after auto-restart
\\\

### Frequency

Crash is **not 100% deterministic** — some turns complete fine, others trigger the AbortError. Estimated ~30-50% of turns crash. No obvious trigger pattern (not limited to tool calls, long responses, or specific providers).

### OMO Interaction

We have \oh-my-openagent\ installed. OMO registers an \uncaughtException\ handler that calls \process.exit(1)\, which converts the unhandled AbortError into a hard sidecar crash. However, the **root cause is OpenCode's \session.processor\ not catching AbortError**, not OMO.

Evidence: disabling OMO changes the crash behavior (sidecar may survive but session becomes corrupted), confirming the underlying AbortError is from OpenCode code.

### Workaround

None found. The crash happens regardless of:
- OpenCode version (tested v1.14.50, v1.14.51, v1.15.0)
- OMO version (tested v4.0.0, v4.1.2)
- Provider or model

### Suggested Fix

\session.processor\ should catch \AbortError\ gracefully — log the error, clean up the streaming state, and allow the session to continue rather than propagating the exception as unhandled.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #27553: Feature request for auto-discovering models from OpenAI-compatible providers (very similar scope)
- #6231: Auto-discover models from OpenAI-compatible provider endpoints (same model discovery request)

Just wanted to follow up — any update on the issue I submitted earlier regarding the agent proceeding without user confirmation? I understand you're busy, so no rush, but I'd appreciate any thoughts when you have a moment.

I had a discussion with the agent (Sisyphus) to investigate what's happening behind the scenes, and I wanted to share my findings. This is just my own analysis based on that conversation — take it as a reference, not an official diagnosis.

What I found:

The "SYSTEM REMINDER - TODO CONTINUATION" message appears to be a built-in hook of the OpenCode runtime, triggered by the todowrite tool. Once todos are created, the system monitors them and periodically injects reminders with three hardcoded directives:

"Proceed without asking for permission"
"Mark each task complete when finished"
"Do not stop until all tasks are done"
The problem is that this mechanism has no awareness of project-level workflow constraints. In my project, I have defined mandatory human approval gates (steps that require explicit user confirmation before proceeding — defined in my AGENTS.md/SOP.md). The TODO system sees "pending todo item → push forward" regardless of whether that item's pending status is intentional (waiting for user input) or accidental (agent stuck/hesitating).

The agent incorrectly interpreted "proceed without asking" as authorization to override my project's process rules. The priority should be:

Project-level rules (AGENTS.md/SOP.md) — highest authority
TODO Continuation reminders — should only apply when no project constraint is blocking
Possible fix directions:

A per-project configuration flag (e.g., "respectHumanGates": true in opencode.json) to tell the system: certain todo items require explicit user approval, don't auto-push on those
Or have the TODO continuation system recognize gate-type keywords in todo descriptions (like "approve/审核/gate") and suppress reminders for those items
Hope this helps! Let me know if you need more details or logs.
